egress.summary: Egress (sprinklered, BCBC 2024 Part 3): pass; 29 floors: 29 pass; the core's two exits are a scissor stair, its doors on the core's opposite faces, 14.0 m apart as smoke would go round the core (3.4.2.3.(3)); the two stairs need a smoke-tight fire separation between them, rated as the floors, with no openings.

assumptions.note: gross unit area over net: walls and the entry, 8% at this stage (the net areas already carry the suggestion's 10% design allowance)
a double-loaded corridor, the wider of the two usual widths
one bay across the plate at its centre for two stairs, the elevator and risers

an elevator shaft with its walls: a core holds one elevator beside its stairs, and one more for each 2.6 m it runs longer than the core bay (its depth across the corridor counts, so a 7 m core 11 m deep holds two)
mechanical, electrical, garbage and recycling on the ground floor
a bicycle space with its aisle share
indoor amenity, at least 40 m²; a placeholder until the operator's brief
a below-grade stall with its aisle share; not on the plates
one window per unit on the elevation, the unit module as the rhythm
one exit stair's width along the core; a core at least one core bay wide holds two stairs at its ends
the shallowest strip a point tower lays homes in, round its ringed core; a home this shallow runs long along the facade
the deepest a home runs back from its window wall before the back of it has no daylight; a placeholder, and the reason a deep plate takes its corridor the other way or wants a courtyard
an entry lobby on the street side of the ground floor, where the building is entered; a placeholder until the architect draws the entry
a leftover of a ground-floor room narrower than this along the strip is not drawn: the room is that much smaller and the notes say so

area_schedule.note: Homes are counted net of their partitions (8% of a home's gross is its walls, shown apart); a home over more than one floor is counted once, on its entry floor.
